source.notes: Scanned school paper (no text layer apart from the icseboard.org watermark); OCR corrected against the page images. Printed header: Grade IX, Assessment I, English Literature, Paper - II, Time: 2 Hours, M.M: 80. No year is printed; examYear 2024 is taken from the file name (...-030424-2024) and the icseboard.org folder. No school name printed. Section A (Question 1, sixteen MCQs) carries only the group mark [16] and is kept as one entry with the options in the text. Sections B (Drama: Julius Caesar, Q2-Q3), C (Prose: Treasure Chest, Q4-Q5) and D (Poetry: Treasure Chest, Q6-Q7): candidates attempt one question from each of B, C and D plus one more, so the pack total (112) exceeds the 80 maximum by design. Each extract (all short) is reproduced in the first part of its question. The taxonomy has no literature chapters for ICSE Class 9 English (only composition, letter-writing, notice-and-email-writing, comprehension-and-summary, functional-grammar, listening-and-speaking-skills), so every entry has chapter null. Paper's own spellings and missing opening quotation marks are kept as printed. No answer key.

questions.sectionTitle: SECTION A (Attempt all questions from this Section.)
questions.text:
Choose the correct answers to the questions from the given options.
(Do not copy the questions, write the correct answers only.)
Select the correct option for each of the following questions:
(i) The first person Casca meets on the stormy night is
(a) Cassius (b) Cicero (c) Cinna (d) Brutus
(ii) The crown was offered to Caesar by the
(a) Mob (b) Senate (c) Mark Antony (d) Casca
(iii) Caesar had a fever in
(a) Egypt (b) Spain (c) Philippi (d) Sardis
(iv) Marullus addresses the citizens to be
(a) blocks (b) stones (c) worse than senseless things (d) all of the above
(v) The bird of night hooted and shrieked in the
(a) Senate House (b) upon Caesar house (c) upon the market place (d) in the Capitol
(vi) According to Trevor, an artist's heart is in his
(a) mind (b) head (c) soul (d) feelings
(vii) Hughie's father has bequeathed him a History of the Peninsular war in fifteen volumes and
(a) beautiful bunglow (b) cavalry sword (c) ten thousand pounds (d) gun
(viii) How much money was offered to the person who would take Oliver Twist?
(a) ten pounds (b) five pounds (c) one pound (d) four pounds
(ix) Where was Oliver Twist born?
(a) in a private clinic (b) in the workhouse (c) in a park (d) in a discarded building
(x) According to Sripati Babu if someone from a different planet came to earth, he would land in....
(a) India (b) some eastern country (c) USA (d) some western country
(xi) Why are women's feet bound in some cultures?
(a) to punish women (b) to make women slaves (c) to make women realize their unimportance (d) to make them small and look attractive
(xii) Which of these statements is NOT true?
(a) Women are themselves responsible for their plight in society.
(b) Women are conditioned to willingly accept stereotypical roles.
(c) The gardener represents the stereotypical male.
(d) Women need to protest against their suppression.
(xiii) Which of these would you associate with Skimble ?
(a) duty-conscious (b) silly (c) intruding (d) dictatorial
(xiv) 'And thought the air must rush as fresh
To swallows on the wing.'
Which figure of speech is used in these lines?
(a) Simile (b) Metaphor (c) Irony (d) Oxymoron
(xv) 'That is so heavy now'. What does 'heavy' refer to here?
(a) the poet's spirit now (b) the swing (c) the poet's spirit in childhood (d) old days of childhood
(xvi) Caesar was deaf from
(a) the left ear (b) the right ear (c) both ears (d) not deaf

questions.sectionTitle: SECTION C - PROSE - SHORT STORIES (Treasure Chest - A Collection of ICSE Poems and Short Stories)
questions.text:
Read the following extract from Oscar Wilde's short story, 'The Model Millionaire' and answer the question that follow:
The old man started, and a faint smile flitted across his withered lips. Thank you, sir,' he said, 'thank you.'
Then Trevor arrived, and Hughie took his leave, blushing a little at what he had done. He spent the day with Laura, got a charming scolding for his extravagance, and had to walk home.
That night he strolled into the Palette Club about eleven o'clock, and found Trevor sitting by himself in the smoking-room drinking hock and seltzer.
Well, Alan, did you get the picture finished all right?' he said, as he lit his cigarette.
What happened that made the old man smile?

questions.sectionTitle: SECTION C - PROSE - SHORT STORIES (Treasure Chest - A Collection of ICSE Poems and Short Stories)
questions.text:
Read the following extract from Charles Dickens short story, 'Oliver Asks for More' and answer the questions that follow:
No one was able to discover who the baby's father was, or what his mother's name was. Mr Bumble, an important officer in the town, invented a name for the baby. He chose the name Oliver Twist.
We name the new babies here in order from A to Z,' he explained when people asked. 'I named the last one Swubble. This one is Twist. The next one will be Unwin'.
At the age of nine, Oliver was a pale, thin child. He and the other workhouse boys never had enough warm clothes or food. They were given only three meals of thin soup every day. On Sundays they had a small piece of bread.
What were the organisers of the workhouse not able to find out?

questions.sectionTitle: SECTION D - POETRY (Treasure Chest - A Collection of ICSE Poems and Short Stories)
questions.text:
Read the following extract from T.S. Eliot's poem, 'Skimbleshanks: The Railway Cat' and answer the questions that follow:
Oh, it's very pleasant when you have found your little den
With your name written up on the door.
And the berth is very neat with a newly folded sheet
And there's not a speck of dust on the floor.
There is every sort of light-you can make it dark or bright:
There's funny little basin you're supposed to wash your face in
And a crank to shut the window if you sneeze.
What does 'little den' signify? How is it made cosy?

questions.sectionTitle: SECTION D - POETRY (Treasure Chest - A Collection of ICSE Poems and Short Stories)
questions.text:
Read the following extract from Thomas Hood's poem, 'I Remember, I Remember' and answer the questions that follow:
I remember, I remember,
Where I was used to swing,
And thought the air must rush as fresh
To swallows on the wing:
My spirit flew in feathers then,
That is so heavy now,
And summer pools could hardly cool
The fever on my brow!
What did the poet's brother plant, and when? What is so exciting about it?
